title: For / since
note: ROUGH STUB 2026-09-01. for = period, since = point. Czech I live here five years. Not PP vs past (B1). a2_present_perfect already uses for as a tense cue — this unit owns which word. Sort period/point. Use = correct.

items.en: I have lived here for two years.
items.gap: I have lived here ____ two years.
accepts: I have lived here for two years.
I've lived here for two years.
items.wrong: I have lived here since two years.

accepts: I have lived here since 2019.
I've lived here since 2019.

items.en: She has worked here for a long time.
items.gap: She has worked here ____ a long time.
accepts: She has worked here for a long time.
She's worked here for a long time.
items.wrong: She has worked here since a long time.

items.en: She has worked here since Monday.
accepts: She has worked here since Monday.
She's worked here since Monday.
items.wrong: She has worked here for Monday.

items.en: We have been here for three days.
items.gap: We have been here ____ three days.
accepts: We have been here for three days.
We've been here for three days.
items.wrong: We have been here since three days.

items.en: We have been here since ten o'clock.
items.gap: We have been here ____ ten o'clock.
accepts: We have been here since ten o'clock.
We've been here since ten o'clock.
items.wrong: We have been here for ten o'clock.

items.en: He has known her for a week.
items.gap: He has known her ____ a week.
accepts: He has known her for a week.
He's known her for a week.
items.wrong: He has known her since a week.

items.en: He has known her since last year.
items.gap: He has known her ____ last year.
accepts: He has known her since last year.
He's known her since last year.
items.wrong: He has known her for last year.

items.en: I have lived here for five years.
items.gap: I have lived here ____ five years.
accepts: I have lived here for five years.
I've lived here for five years.
items.wrong: I have lived here since five years.

accepts: I have lived here since 2020.
I've lived here since 2020.

cards.title: For / since
points: **for** and **since** say how long something has been true.
**for** is a period — beginning and ending: **for two years**.
Czech often uses present and no word: *Bydlím tady pět let.*
